paragraphs: We track more than a dozen restaurants in Austin, from fast-food chains to bowl-and-salad concepts, and each one has menu data on file. The single highest-protein dish in our Austin data is the Triple Meat Whataburger, at 1,070 calories and 65g of protein. Snap Kitchen's Large Bison Quinoa Bowl is next, at 830 calories and 57g of protein.

Outside that pair, protein density clusters lower: Modern Market Eatery's Bacon Jam Club is 670 calories with 49g of protein, and Flower Child's Green Chile Beef Colorado Bowl is 750 calories with 47g of protein. Chick-fil-A's Cool Wrap, at 660 calories and 43g of protein, is one of the leaner fast-food options we've logged for the city. Whole Foods Market's Texas Athlete Bowl is smaller across the board at 475 calories with 45g of protein — close to matching the bowl chains on protein while using fewer calories to get there.

When comparing two dishes, don't stop at protein grams; check the calorie total too. A 450-calorie bowl with 45g of protein delivers more protein per calorie than a 1,000-calorie plate with 55g, even though the second number looks bigger on its own.
Whataburger's Triple Meat Whataburger is the highest-protein item we track here: 65g protein, 1070 calories.

new-york.title: 11 Best Healthy Restaurants in New York (2026) — Macros & Calories
new-york.desc: New York's high-protein restaurant meals skew hard toward fast-casual bowls, and the numbers back it up: across the 85 meals we track at 15 New York…
paragraphs: New York's high-protein restaurant meals skew hard toward fast-casual bowls, and the numbers back it up: across the 85 meals we track at 15 New York restaurants, 72 of them clear 30g of protein. That is an unusually high share, and it means the question here is rarely whether a menu has a high-protein option — it is which one gives you the most protein per calorie.

On that measure Chipotle leads. Its Double Chicken Bowl delivers 68g of protein in 560 calories, a ratio no other meal in our New York data matches, and the Double High-Protein Bowl is the outright protein leader in the city at 81g for 760 calories. If you want the same idea in a smaller package, The Little Beet's Grilled Chicken Plate carries 45g in just 420 calories, and Whole Foods Market's High Protein Plate reaches 48g at 460.

The salad and Mediterranean options cluster slightly lower but still land well above a typical restaurant meal. Chopt's Classic Cobb Salad reaches 60g at 600 calories. Pokeworks' large Spicy Ahi Tuna Bowl carries 55g for 790. CAVA's Spicy Chicken + Avocado Pita hits 50g at 980, with its Greek Chicken Pita at 48g, and NAYA's Beef Shawarma High-Protein Bowl reaches 48g. Dig's Power Plate is among the leanest high-protein plates at 42g for 465 calories, and The Little Beet's Steak & Eggs Bowl carries 48g at 540.

The practical pattern across these New York menus: doubling the protein at a build-your-own counter is almost always the cheapest way to move a meal from roughly 25g to 45g or more, and it adds far fewer calories than the equivalent jump from adding a second base or a sauce. Sort the meals below by protein, calories, carbs, or fat to find the ones that fit your targets.

Chipotle Mexican Grill's Double High-Protein Bowl (double adobo chicken + light rice + black beans + fajita veggies + tomato salsa + cheese + romaine) is the highest-protein item we track here: 81g protein, 760 calories.

Ninety-one of the San Diego meals we track clear 30g of protein, so hitting a target in this city is less about finding one particular restaurant than about knowing which item on a familiar menu carries the load. nashville.title: 7 Best Healthy Restaurants in Nashville (2026) — Macros & Calories
nashville.desc: Eating high-protein in Nashville is easier than you might think. We track 7 macro-friendly restaurants here with verified nutrition data — spanning…
paragraphs: Eating high-protein in Nashville is easier than you might think. We track 7 macro-friendly restaurants here with verified nutrition data — spanning mexican, bowls, burritos, wraps, and gluten free options — so you can compare calories and protein before you order, whether you want a quick bowl on the way to the gym or a sit-down plate.

Standouts include Chipotle Mexican Grill, Flower Child, Greenery Co., CAVA, Radish Kitchen, Sweetgreen, and True Food Kitchen. Most lean on grilled and roasted proteins, build-your-own bowls, and fresh sides, so it's easy to hit your numbers without a calorie blowout.

For the best protein-to-calorie ratio, the fast-casual bowl and grill spots are your friends: load up on grilled chicken, steak, falafel, or fish, and go easy on pita, cheese, and creamy dressings. Chipotle Mexican Grill is a dependable high-protein pick in Nashville; double the protein when you need 40g+ in a single meal.

At CAVA, start with a grain or salad base, add a double scoop of grilled chicken or braised lamb, and load up on hummus, lentils, and vegetables; skipping the pita and going light on dressing keeps it lean and high-protein. At Chipotle, a burrito bowl with double chicken (no tortilla) plus fajita veggies, black beans, and salsa is one of the easiest 40g+ protein orders in fast casual. At Sweetgreen, build a warm bowl with blackened chicken or steak over greens and a grain, and take a lighter dressing on the side.

The playbook is the same across Nashville: choose grilled or roasted over fried, prioritize lean protein and vegetables, double the protein when you need 40g or more in one meal, and skip sugary drinks and calorie-dense sauces. Every restaurant below breaks down verified protein, calories, carbs, and fat, so you can plan your order with confidence and track your macros accurately while eating out in Nashville.
